title: Regional surge absorber and transparent fallback proxy
author: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Introduces a light-weight regional "surge absorber" component plus a transparent fallback proxy to reduce cascading circuit flips during short-term capacity spikes. Motivation: We observed two incidents where transient egress pressure in a single region caused rapid circuit state churn and tenant-level mass fallbacks, worsening latency and causing client retries. This PR adds a mitigation that throttles and absorbs brief surges at the routing layer and routes affected requests to a transparent fallback proxy that can serve compatible model variants or alternate capacity tiers.

What changed (high level): - Add an in-router surge-absorber with a token-bucket window and soft-queue to smooth very short spikes (<= 2s). - Introduce transparent-fallback-proxy service that can forward requests to lower-cost compatible variants or regional peers without exposing fallback routing to callers. - Telemetry: new metrics (surge_absorbed_count, fallback_proxy_forward_rate, fallback_latency_ms_p50/p95) and trace tags added to trace the absorber decision path. - Policy: new JSON policy entries enabling per-tenant and per-route softness thresholds (defaults conservative). - Tests: unit + integration harness with synthetic spike replay and a small chaos script.

Behavioral notes: The absorber is conservative by default: it will only buffer up to 100 requests and hold them for up to 2s before allowing fallback. The transparent fallback proxy supports header-based routing so downstream services can still observe original request metadata. No customer-visible API changes.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature-disabled on main; enabled behind feature flag ff.regional_surge_absorber for 10% of traffic in us-west-2 for the first 24h. 2) Observe metrics and error budgets; expand to 50% if p95 latency and SLOs are stable. 3) Ramp globally after 72h with an automatic rollback script if surge_absorbed_count > threshold and fallback latency > 2x baseline.

Testing: Unit tests added for token-bucket math, queue eviction and fallback decision. Integration tests added to perf-canary suite — synthetic sinusoidal spike, and a realistic client-retry pattern. Local annotation harness verifies trace tags are present. CI initially flaked on an e2e due to a timeout in the mock peer; rerun succeeded.

Migration and compatibility: Policy file format extended with a backward compatible optional "soft_window_ms" and "soft_queue_size". Existing policies remain valid. Operators can pre-seed preferred fallback model variants via the operator console.

Risk and fallback: Low to medium. The absorber is opt-in; a buggy path would at worst route to the fallback proxy which currently mirrors the original routing logic. A fast rollback toggle and a region-level circuit unbind are provided.

Related: ENG-4021 (incident postmortem), ENG-4187 (regional routing policy work).
